content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli casserole with noodles is a baked dish that combines fresh broccoli florets with cooked noodles, a creamy sauce and cheese. The meal is rich in B‑vitamins, vitamin C, fiber and protein, and offers a mild, savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is sometimes called “little trees” because its florets resemble tiny crowns.
Casseroles with broccoli became popular in the United States during the 1970s.
Noodles help retain moisture, keeping the casserole tender and juicy.
The creamy sauce is often made from milk and flour, making it lighter than a traditional cheese sauce.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Broccoli provides a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from broccoli aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Together, noodles and broccoli supply a complete set of amino acids useful for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium from cheese and vitamin K from broccoli contribute to strong bones.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Broccoli’s phytochemicals, such as sulforaphane, help combat free radicals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The creamy sauce and cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese can be salty; low‑sodium alternatives are recommended.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Broccoli can cause gas in sensitive individuals; serve in moderate portions.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Cook the noodles until al dente, steam or sauté the broccoli for a few minutes, combine with sauce and cheese, place in a baking dish and bake 20‑25 minutes at 180 °C until golden. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the casserole to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk to keep the sauce from drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Ready-to-eat cereal (NFS) consists of dry grain flakes that have been heat‑treated for instant preparation. It typically contains a blend of wheat, corn and rice, is fortified with vitamins and minerals, and may include dried fruit, nuts or sweeteners.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cereal is ready in minutes – just add milk or water and wait a short time.
There are over 100 flavor variations, from classic "honey‑nut" to exotic "mango‑coconut".
Most ready‑to‑eat cereals are fortified with B‑vitamins, iron and calcium.
Thermal processing makes the flakes crunchy and extends shelf life.
In some countries, ready‑to‑eat cereal is used as a base for energy bars.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fortified cereals provide vitamin D, iron, calcium and folic acid, supporting bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs deliver sustained energy and help maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most ready‑to‑eat cereals contain little saturated fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Whole‑grain ingredients and added fiber improve gut function and regularity.

items.title: Convenient and quick
items.content: Fast preparation helps maintain a regular eating schedule, which is important for busy lifestyles.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties contain high amounts of added sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Most cereals are wheat‑based and contain gluten, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Ingredients may include nuts, soy or dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Certain cereals can cause rapid spikes in blood glucose, which may be undesirable for those with insulin resistance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour milk, kefir, yogurt or a plant‑based drink over the cereal, then add fresh or dried fruit, nuts and honey. It can also serve as a base for smoothie bowls or be incorporated into baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container. Shelf life is indicated on the packaging.

club-sandwich-on-wheat-with-cheese.title: Club sandwich on wheat, with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A club sandwich on wheat bread with cheese consists of three layers of toasted wheat bread, stacked with ham, turkey, bacon, lettuce, tomato and melted cheese. It is served cold or lightly warmed, often cut into halves or quarters.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The club sandwich originated in the United States in the early 1900s and quickly became a staple in diners and cafés.
Traditional recipes use three types of meat, while vegetarian versions replace them with plant‑based alternatives.
Wheat bread gives the sandwich a softer texture compared with white or whole‑grain breads.
Melted cheese is chosen for its ability to bind the ingredients together and add a creamy flavor.
Club sandwiches are commonly served with French fries and pickles on the side.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The meat layers (ham, turkey, bacon) and cheese provide a substantial amount of complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Provides calcium
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and wheat bread supply B1, B2, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat bread and fresh vegetables (lettuce, tomato) add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Iron
items.content: The meat components deliver heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham, bacon and cheese are often salty, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Bacon and processed cheese are rich in saturated fats that may raise cholesterol when consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the combination of bread, meat and cheese, the sandwich is relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is usually cut into quarters and served with fries, a side salad or a dipping sauce. It can be eaten cold or briefly warmed in the oven to melt the cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep a prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the components: keep bread and vegetables apart to prevent sogginess.

egg-whole-fried-no-added-fat.title: Egg, whole, fried no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: A whole egg fried without added fat is a standard chicken egg cooked on a dry skillet. This method retains most nutrients while delivering a low‑calorie, protein‑rich dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most complete foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Frying without oil creates a crisp exterior without extra calories.
Eggs provide more vitamin D than most plant‑based foods.
They are widely used as a binding and leavening agent in cooking.
USDA defines a "large" egg as the standard serving size.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A large egg supplies about 6 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin (B2) and biotin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Choline
items.content: Choline in the yolk is important for liver function and cognitive processes.

items.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These carotenoids help protect eye health and may reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk is high in cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume eggs in moderation.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella. Fry until the white is fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried eggs without added fat can be enjoyed on their own, added to salads, sandwiches, rice or vegetable dishes. Cook on medium heat for a softer texture or high heat for a crispy edge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep eggs refrigerated at 1‑4 °C in their original carton. Use within 3‑5 days of purchase. Cooked eggs should be stored in the fridge and eaten within 2 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Soft Drink "Pepper" is a non‑alcoholic carbonated beverage with a subtle chili pepper heat. It combines the sweetness of sugar, citrus aromatics, and a characteristic spicy note, creating a unique flavor profile. The drink is made from water, sugar, natural flavorings, chili extract, and carbon dioxide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first pepper‑flavored soda was launched in Japan in the early 2000s.
Chili heat is measured on the Scoville scale; the drink typically uses extract rated 500–800 Scoville units, giving a mild yet noticeable kick.
Chili in the drink is considered a natural metabolism stimulant.
It is often served in cocktails as a substitute for traditional bitters.
Carbonation softens the perception of heat compared to pure chili sauce.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Capsaicin, the active component of chili, can increase thermogenesis, helping the body burn more calories.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: The beverage contains vitamin C and polyphenols that help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Mild spiciness stimulates gastric juice production, aiding nutrient absorption.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Capsaicin may trigger endorphin release, creating a mild sense of well‑being.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any carbonated drink, it contributes to the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Sensitivity to spice
items.content: People with a low tolerance for heat or with gastritis should consume the drink in moderation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The soda contains sugar, so individuals with diabetes or those monitoring calorie intake should limit consumption.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbon dioxide can cause bloating in some individuals.

items.title: Chili allergy
items.content: Rarely, an allergic reaction to chili components may occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Soft Drink "Pepper" chilled over ice. It can be used as a base for cocktails, mixed with fruit juices, or added to meat marinades for a gentle heat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Soursop (Graviola) is a tropical fruit known for its aromatic, mildly sweet flavor with hints of pineapple and citrus. The nectar is made from ripe fruits, stripped of seeds, and diluted with water and sugar, creating a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soursop grows in tropical regions of South America, the Caribbean, and Southeast Asia.
In traditional medicine, the fruit and leaves have been used to support immunity and digestion.
The fruit is a rich source of vitamin C – over 30 mg per 100 g of product.
The nectar is often served chilled and is popular in summer cocktails and desserts.
Soursop has a soft, creamy texture, making it an ideal base for smoothies.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and anthocyanins in soursop help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber present in the nectar promotes healthy digestion and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The nectar is high in water content, aiding overall fluid balance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many fruit juices, soursop nectar contains virtually no fat.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to soursop, manifested as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Nectar is often sweetened, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Seed toxicity
items.content: Soursop seeds contain compounds that can be toxic in large amounts; they are removed during nectar production.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soursop nectar can be enjoyed chilled, used in cocktails, smoothies, dessert sauces, or as a base for fruit punches. It can also be diluted with water or mixed with sparkling water for a lighter drink.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the nectar in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.

stuffed-shells-cheese-and-spinach-filled.title: Stuffed shells, cheese- and spinach-filled, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells are large pasta shells filled with a mixture of cheese and spinach. They are sold without sauce, making them convenient for quick snacks or adding to salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally these shells are baked in Italian cuisine, often under a tomato sauce.
The combination of cheese (usually ricotta or mozzarella) and spinach provides a pleasant balance of flavor and texture.
Without sauce the product is easier to store and transport, requiring no additional reheating.
Spinach retains most of its vitamins when the product is flash‑frozen after preparation.
In some countries the shells are used as a base for vegetarian meals.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The cheese in the filling supplies high‑quality animal protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and spinach contain B2, B6 and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese provides calcium, which contributes to bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Spinach is high in lutein and vitamin C, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Spinach adds fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared stuffed shells can contain added salt, which should be considered on low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of cheese and pasta, the dish is relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shells can be eaten cold in a salad, reheated in a microwave or oven, added to soups, or used as part of sandwich spreads. They pair well with olive oil, fresh herbs, or a light yogurt dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in its original packaging in the refrigerator at 0 °C‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. For freezing, place in an airtight bag and store up to 2 months. Discard if any off‑odor or mold appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Carbonated flavored water is a non‑alcoholic beverage made by saturating pure water with carbon dioxide and adding natural or artificial flavorings. It contains no sugar, no calories, and is often used as an alternative to sweet soft drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial brand of flavored carbonated water appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Flavorings can be natural (citrus, berries) or artificial, mimicking fruit tastes.
Dissolved carbon dioxide creates a mild tingling sensation that enhances flavor perception.
In some countries, flavored carbonated water is classified as “mineral water” if it contains certain minerals.

items.title: Sugar‑free hydration
items.content: Helps maintain body water balance without added calories or sugar, which is beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Moderate consumption may help relieve constipation by gently stimulating stomach motility.

items.title: Reduces sweet cravings
items.content: Flavored taste can diminish the desire for sugary drinks, supporting healthier eating habits.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Carbonated water has a lower pH, which with frequent use may contribute to tooth enamel erosion.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored versions contain added sodium, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Artificial flavorings
items.content: Certain individuals may experience allergic reactions or sensitivity to artificial flavor compounds.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink chilled, use as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails, incorporate in cooking to add light fizz to batters, or mix with fruit juices for refreshing mocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the bottle tightly sealed. After opening, consume within 2–3 days to retain carbonation.
